_readme: Every row states where OUR claim can be checked (our_proof, a command that exists in this repo) and how much we actually know about the other side (competitor_status). Statuses: observed = we looked and a source is given; inferred = our reasoning, not a measurement; unverified = we looked and did not find a public example, or we did not look — search_note must say which. A claim about a competitor may only be published as fact when status is observed AND a source is given.

edges.dimension: does the verdict call a model
edges.our_claim: Verdicts are pure functions: no network, no model, byte-identical across reruns.
edges.competitor_note: Guardrail products generally classify free text with a model. We measured none of them; the cost claim is therefore about our input shape, not their throughput.
edges.search_note: Searched 2026-11-19 for open-source medical-device change-assessment engines; results were FDA 510(k) records plus one peer project whose charter does not describe model usage. No latency measurement of any product was obtained.
edges.risk: If read as a speed comparison against LLM guardrails it is a category error: they judge language, we judge a structured context.

edges.dimension: does each rule name its legal basis
edges.our_claim: All 60 rules carry a LAW or DOCTRINE label, with DOCTRINE capped at 12.
edges.competitor_note: OpenOnco documents a 'transparent YAML rule engine, not opaque ML' — so rule transparency is NOT unique to us. Its charter makes no claim about per-rule clause citations, but we did not read its rules in full.
edges.search_note: Read romeo111/OpenOnco CHARTER.md on 2026-11-19: transparent YAML rules, and an explicit statement that technical checks are not clinical validation.
edges.risk: Transparency exists elsewhere. Our narrower, defensible difference is clause-level citation plus a machine check that no rule lacks a basis — not 'we are the only auditable one'.

edges.dimension: is the evaluation report generated or written
edges.our_claim: The report is emitted by the evaluator and a check fails when its numbers disagree with the repo.
edges.competitor_note: OpenOnco's charter commits to recording 'actual technical verification and unresolved content limitations', but says nothing about whether that record is generated or hand-written. We could not determine this from outside.
edges.search_note: Read the peer charter on 2026-11-19; it states a process obligation, not a mechanism. Nothing public showed whether its reports are derived from runs.
edges.risk: Our own drift (40/26 -> 54/30) is the only drift we can evidence; peers may already do this and we would not know.

edges.our_claim: Nine intentionally unencoded clauses are published with a status and a reason.
edges.competitor_note: OpenOnco publishes scope limits and 'changes requiring a new scope assessment' — publishing boundaries is also not unique. Its list is human-readable prose; ours is machine-checked with a status enum.
edges.search_note: Read the peer charter on 2026-11-19; it lists five scope constraints and the change types that trigger reassessment.
edges.risk: Nine published gaps may be more than a competitor has; publishing is not the same as having few.

edges.dimension: can an outsider re-run the claims
edges.our_claim: Twenty checks run from a fresh clone with no credentials.
edges.competitor_note: Solo-maintainer peer projects often rely on their own CI. We did not inspect any peer's test setup closely enough to say whether an outsider can reproduce its claims.
edges.search_note: Searched 2026-11-19; the peer's public charter makes no statement about reproducing verification from a clean clone.
edges.risk: Reproducibility is a property of our repo today, not a permanent lead.

edges.dimension: are the claims enforced in public CI
edges.our_claim: 58 contract assertions run on every push, including the three laws.
edges.competitor_note: We did not audit any peer's CI configuration, nor whether its assertions cover behavioural laws rather than exit codes.
edges.search_note: Not inspected on 2026-11-19; this row requires opening a peer repository's workflow files, which we did not do.
edges.risk: A green CI badge proves assertions pass, not that the assertions are the right ones.

edges.dimension: is the scope limited to enumerated categories
edges.our_claim: Anything outside the tables returns hold; coverage is the bottleneck, stated as such.
edges.competitor_note: General-purpose guardrails aim at open-ended text, so their scope is wider and shallower by design; the peer we read targets clinical decision support and explicitly disclaims device classification.
edges.search_note: Compared scopes on 2026-11-19 from the peer charter: it declares an intended use in clinician-facing decision support and disclaims any regulatory classification.
edges.risk: Wider scope may be the better product for a user who needs to catch something we never enumerated.
